intro: Celtic forward Yang Hyun-jun has added another key moment to his early career with a critical goal in the match against St Mirren. However, the Bhoys will now face the challenge of competing without his services as Yang departs to represent his country at the Asian Games. As Celtic eye continuing success in both domestic and European competitions, the absence of one of their emerging players raises questions about the team's depth and adaptability in the weeks ahead.

sections.heading: Yang Hyun-jun's Impact on Celtic
sections.text: Yang Hyun-jun, the South Korean forward, has quickly started to make his presence felt at Celtic Park. His goal against St Mirren came at a pivotal moment, further demonstrating his ability to thrive under pressure. Players like Yang are vital in a squad aiming for dominance in the Scottish Premiership while juggling commitments in European competitions. His pace, skill, and contribution to the attack have made him an increasingly reliable option for manager Brendan Rodgers, who returned to the club during the summer.

sections.heading: The Asian Games and its Importance
sections.text: The Asian Games is a major sporting event held every four years, featuring athletes from across Asia competing in a variety of disciplines. While often overlooked in Europe, the football competition is highly prestigious in Asia, offering an opportunity for younger talents to shine on the international stage. Yang Hyun-jun’s participation is a significant moment in his career, as it could serve to further establish him as a key figure for South Korea. For Celtic, however, his temporary absence poses a test of squad depth and resilience as the fixtures pile up in what is always a demanding season for the Glasgow giants.

analysis: Yang Hyun-jun's recent performances underline his growing importance to Celtic as they aim to stay at the top of the Scottish Premiership and make an impact in continental tournaments. His instrumental role in the game against St Mirren will have solidified his place as a rising star within Brendan Rodgers' squad. Yet, his early departure to the Asian Games is a timely reminder of the challenges faced by managers during the season, as key players are often called away for international duties. This could be an opportunity for other members of the team to step up and showcase their abilities, keeping Celtic's momentum alive despite this key absence. Balancing such absences is a hallmark of successful clubs, and how Celtic navigates this scenario will be worth watching in the coming weeks.
